info.title: mtdl-web
info.summary: Search, download and subscribe to the German public broadcasters' media libraries.
info.description:
Everything mtdl-web's own interface does goes through this API, so scripts and other services can do it too.

**Base path** `/api/v1`, JSON in and out. Film ids travel as strings: JavaScript numbers lose precision beyond 2^53.

**Authentication.** Send an API key in the header `X-Api-Key`; keys are created in the settings under *Access*. A
read key may call every `GET` and the previews (`POST` routes that change nothing), a write key everything. A read
key asking for a change gets `403` with the code `api_key_read_only`. Without a key the access mode decides; with a
password that is the browser's session cookie, which is meant for the interface, not for scripts.

**Errors** carry an object in `detail` with a machine-readable `code`, sometimes with more fields:
`{"detail": {"code": "subscription_not_found"}}`, `{"detail": {"code": "library_in_use", "subscriptions": [3]}}`.
Input that does not fit the schema answers `422` with FastAPI's list of validation errors in `detail`.
A change a browser marks as coming from another site is refused with `403` and the code `cross_site`; scripts send
no such headers. Without sign-in (access mode `none`), requests without a key are answered only under an IP address
or a local name, otherwise with `403` and the code `host_not_local`.

Events reach other services as webhooks or hook scripts; assistants use the MCP server at `/mcp` (off by default).

get.description:
For the container health check: cheap, writes nothing (a write test would keep array disks awake).
503 when degraded, so Docker marks the container unhealthy; the UI still works and shows the problems.
Open without sign-in, so only what is wrong: paths, library names and error texts are in /api/v1/status.
Open without sign-in: the UI decides from it whether to show the setup, the sign-in or itself.

post.description: The first password, with the one-time code from the container log.

Change the password; other sessions end. The first one comes from /auth/setup with the code from the log,
also in mode local: being in the own network is not enough to claim the password that counts from outside.
Sign out everywhere else (a lost phone, a shared computer).

get.description: What runs where, sizes and free space: for the settings page and bug reports (no secrets).

``q`` understands the MediathekViewWeb syntax: ``!sender``, ``#thema``, ``+titel``, ``*beschreibung``,
``>minuten``, ``<minuten``, commas join words that must all occur. ``scope`` all (or ``description``) also searches
descriptions; ``status`` adds what mtdl-web knows per hit.

post.description: Write test on demand (settings page, first start).
Target paths of example films under a naming scheme: the live example in the settings.

get.description:
``order=queue`` lists in the order downloads start (for the queue), else newest first; ``subscription``
only that subscription's (the counts stay those of all downloads).

post.description:
Cancels everything waiting or loading, or only one subscription's downloads. The ids allow an undo
(``/downloads/{id}/retry``).
Where ``POST /downloads`` would put the film, without queueing it: the preview of the download dialog.

delete.summary: Remove a download from the history
delete.description: Removes the entry (history); files stay where they are.

post.summary: Move a download in the queue
post.description: Changes the order of the queue; only waiting downloads can move.
``subscription``: the saved subscription the draft edits; its skipped episodes show as skipped.

delete.description: Downloads stay in the history (and on disk); they only lose the link to the subscription.
Releases the skipped episodes: the next check loads them like any other match.

post.description: Checks every active subscription now (otherwise this runs after each film list update).

post.summary: Load failed and cancelled episodes again
post.description:
Loads the subscription's failed and cancelled episodes again: they leave the history, a check queues them
with today's naming and quality. ``forgotten``: history entries removed, ``queued``: downloads queued.

get.description: Whether the tokens of the library features are set (never their values).
Series on TMDB for a name, for assigning a subscription to its series.
Movies on TMDB for a title, for a single download into a movie library.
The movie as a download names it; ``library_id``: the movie library to look for its folders in.

The series as the subscription uses it; ``refresh`` asks TMDB again (new episodes listed there);
``library_id``: the series library to look for its folders in (default: the only one).

post.summary: Preview the paths of a library
post.description:
Paths under a library template, relative to the library: a regular episode and a special, or a movie. The
live example of the library form.

put.description: A new path moves the library: downloads in it keep their place relative to it (move the files along).

delete.description: Files stay where they are. Refused while subscriptions or unfinished downloads use the library.

post.description: A key for scripts, other services and assistants (MCP): header X-Api-Key, in every access mode.

Download history and subscriptions of the MediathekView desktop app: first as a dry run, then with
``apply``. Downloads count as done (subscriptions skip them), subscriptions arrive paused.

get.description:
A read-only API key gets only scheme and host of each url, and `***` for a body template: both often carry
a token.

post.description: Sends a ``webhook.test`` event once and answers with the result.

get.description:
The channel's logo when the setting ``channel_logos`` is on and the MediathekView project has one; 404 otherwise
(the UI shows the name instead).

The logo a data source asks to show with its notice (TMDB), served from here: the browser loads nothing
from elsewhere.

Scripts in the hooks folder (``<event>.d/``) and their last run. Read only: scripts come from the config
folder alone, the API neither writes nor starts one.

put.description: Inside a schedule window: ``paused`` opens the limit until the window ends; false returns to the schedule.

get.description: Everything the status bar shows, in one request (the UI polls it every few seconds).

AppSettings.title: AppSettings
AppSettings.description: Settings the user changes at runtime. New fields need a default: stored documents may lack them.

FilmIn.title: FilmIn
FilmIn.description: A film from a search result, for sources other than the local film list (MediathekViewWeb).

FilmStatusOut.title: FilmStatusOut
FilmStatusOut.description:
What mtdl-web knows about a search hit: downloaded (also as the same broadcast on another channel),
waiting, loading, and which subscription it would belong to.

SecretsIn.title: SecretsIn
SecretsIn.description: Only the fields sent change; null or "" removes the stored token.

secret.title: Secret
secret.description: Signs the body. On update: null keeps the stored one, '' removes it.

headers.title: Headers
headers.description: Own headers, e.g. an API key. On update: null keeps all stored ones, an object replaces them; a header with the value null keeps its stored value.

body_template.title: Body Template
body_template.description: Replaces the default JSON body. Placeholders: {{event}}, {{time}}, {{data.<field>}}.

api_key.description: An API key from the settings (Access). A read key may call GET and the previews, a write key all.
api_key.name: X-Api-Key
